## 1 Preparations

### 1.1 Obtain the information and endpoint of an API operation

**endpoint of an API operation**

To call an API operation by using an SDK, you must obtain the information about the API operation, including the service code, API operation name, and API version.

**Background information**

The information on the API directory page of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console is for reference only. For more information about how to call API operations, see the developer guides of cloud services. If the information on the API directory page is different from that in the developer guide of a cloud service, the information in the developer guide prevails.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Development Tools** > **API & SDK** >
**OpenAPI Explorer**.
3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, choose **API Integration** > **API Debugging** in the top
navigation bar.
4. In the upper-left corner, move the pointer over the More icon and then select the cloud
service whose API operation you want to call.
5. Select an API version from the **Version** drop-down list.
6. In the API operation list, you can view all API operations of the current version.
7. Click the API operation that you want to call. Obtain the endpoint from the Endpoint
parameter on the Parameter tab.

### 1.2 Obtain AccessKey credentials

AccessKey credentials are assigned by Resource Access Management (RAM) or Security Token Service (STS). You can use one of the preceding types of AccessKey credentials for authentication when you call API operations.

**Background information**

An AccessKey pair is used to verify the identity of a request sender based on symmetric encryption. An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. The AccessKey ID is used to identify a user. The AccessKey secret is used to encrypt the signature string. AccessKey credentials can be assigned by RAM or STS: An AccessKey pair that is assigned by RAM to a third party consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. An AccessKey 3-tuple that is assigned by STS to a third party consists of an AccessKey ID, an AccessKey secret, and a security token. rations

**Obtain an AccessKey pair**

The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides two types of AccessKey pairs: those for personal accounts and those for organization accounts. We recommend that you use AccessKey pairs for personal accounts to call the API operations of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and cloud services.

> **Note:** Only operations administrators and level-1 organization administrators can obtain AccessKey pairs for organization accounts.

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account**

To use AccessKey pairs for personal accounts, you must configure the header parameters that are described in the following table for access control. Otherwise, an error that indicates insufficient permissions may occur.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| x-acs-regionid | The ID of the region to which the instance that you want to access belongs. Example: cn- qingdao-****-****. |
| x-acs-organizationid | The ID of the organization to which the instance that you want to access belongs. For information about how to obtain the ID, see the "Obtain an organization ID" section of the Obtain the values of common request headers topic. |
| x-acs-resourcegroupid | The ID of the resource set to which the instance that you want to access belongs. For information about how to obtain the ID, see the "Obtain a resource set ID" section of the Obtain the values of common request headers topic. |
| x-acs-instanceid | The ID of the instance that you want to access. For example, you can view the ID of an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance in the ECS instance list. |

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the upper-right corner of the homepage, click the profile picture and then click **User**
**Information**.
3. In the **AccessKey Pair** section, view the AccessKey pair of the personal account.
rations

> **Note:** The AccessKey pair provides full access to cloud resources within your Alibaba Cloud account. You must keep the AccessKey pair confidential.

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization**

> **Warning:** The AccessKey pair of a personal account is managed by the permission system of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. If you need to obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, make sure that your operation is allowed by an administrator. This ensures security.

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Resources > Organizations**.
4. In the organization list, click the name of the level-1 organization whose AccessKey pair you
want to obtain.
5. On the right side of the page that appears, click **Management AccessKey**.
6. In the dialog box that appears, view the AccessKey pair of the organization.

Find the cluster and click **Cluster Details** in the **Actions** column. v. On the cluster details page, click the **Desired State Configuration** tab. vi. In the list of files displayed on the left, click **kv.conf**. Then, click **Show Content** on the right. Press Ctrl+F and search for `region` and `internet-domain` to obtain their values. rations

```java
private static String callAssumeRole(IAcsClient client) {
    CommonRequest request = new CommonRequest();
    // Replace "sts.aliyuns.com" with the endpoint of STS. The format of an endpoint
is sts-vpc.${global:region}.${global:internet-domain}.
    request.setSysDomain("<sts.aliyuns.com>");
    request.setSysProduct("Sts");
    request.setSysAction("AssumeRole");
    request.setSysVersion("2015-04-01");
    request.setSysMethod(MethodType.POST);
    request.setHttpContentType(FormatType.FORM);
    // The name of the role session. You can specify this parameter based on your bus
iness requirements. This parameter is usually set to the identity of the user who cal ls the API operation, such as the username. Replace "<yourRoleSessionName>" with your custom value.
    request.putQueryParameter("RoleSessionName", "<yourRoleSessionName>");
    // The ARN of the RAM role. This role is a RAM role whose trusted entity is an AS
CM user. Replace "<yourRoleArn>" with the actual RAM role obtained in the first step.
    request.putQueryParameter("RoleArn", "<yourRoleArn>");
    try {
        CommonResponse response = client.getCommonResponse(request);
        return response.getData();
    } catch (ServerException e) {
        System.out.println(e.getErrCode());
        System.out.println(e.getErrMsg());
    } catch (ClientException e) {
        System.out.println(e.getErrCode());
        System.out.println(e.getErrMsg());
```

### 1.3 Obtain the values of common request headers

**request headers**

In Apsara Stack, you must specify multiple common request headers to call API operations. Then, common response parameters are returned in the results.

**Common request parameters**

You must specify the common request parameters in the code to call API operations in Apsara Stack. For example, you must replace `<yourResourceGroupID>` with the actual resource set ID in

```
 request.putHeadParameter("x-acs-resourcegroupid", "<yourResourceGroupID>")  when you
```

use SDK for Java to call API operations.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| x-acs-regionid | The ID of the region in which the instance resource on which you want to perform operations resides. For more information, see the Obtain a region ID section of this topic. |
| x-acs-organizationid | The ID of the organization to which the instance resource on which you want to perform operations belongs. For more information, see the Obtain an organization ID section of this topic. |
| x-acs-resourcegroupid | The ID of the resource set to which the instance resource on which you want to perform operations belongs. For more information, see the Obtain a resource set ID section of this topic. |
| x-acs-instanceid | The ID of the instance to which the resource on which you want to perform operations belongs. For more information, see the Obtain an instance ID section of this topic. |

rations

| Note When you call API operations of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, you do not need to use the x-acs-organizationid , x-acs-resourcegroupid , and x- acs-instanceid parameters. When you call API operations of other cloud services in Apsara Stack, you must use the <x-acs-organizationid> parameter to specify the organization ID to the request header. Otherwise, the call fails and an error message is returned, which indicates that you do not have permissions to initiate calls. When you call API operations of other cloud services in Apsara Stack, we recommend that you use the <x-acs-resourcegroupid> parameter to specify the resource set ID to the request header. After you specify the organization ID and the resource set ID, you can narrow down the query scope when you query instance resources. If you do not use the <x-acs-resourcegroupid> parameter to specify the resource set ID, the default resource set of the organization to which the user belongs is used. |   |   |

## 2 Use POP to make API calls

### 2.1 Obtain the endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console

**Apsara Uni-manager Management**

**Console**

To obtain the endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, you can obtain the values of required variables in the Apsara Infrastructure Management console based on the configuration format of the endpoint and then concatenate the values. You can also search for the endpoint in the Apsara Infrastructure Management console.

**Background information**

To use the Portable OpenAPI Proxy (POP) gateway to call API operations in Apsara Stack, you must obtain required service endpoints. You can obtain service endpoints from Apsara Stack onsite O&M engineers or by using one of the following methods.

**Method 1: Concatenate variable values to generate an**

**endpoint**

You can obtain the values of required variables and concatenate the values based on the configuration format of the endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Configuration format of the endpoint in the central region: **ascm.${global:internet-**

**domain}**

Configuration format of the endpoint in the general region:

**ascm.${global:region}.${global:internet-domain}**

> **Note:** ${global:internet-domain} and ${global:region} are variables and need to be replaced with the actual values that you obtained. ${global:} is not included in the final endpoint.

**Obtain actual values of variables**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Platform O&M** > **Apsara Infrastructure Management**
> **Resources**. The **Product & Cluster O&M** page appears.

3. Enter **ascm-A** in the **Product | Cluster** search box on the **Product & Cluster O&M**
page, find the ascm-A-xxx cluster, and then click **Cluster Details** in the Actions column.
4. On the **cluster details** page, click the **Desired State Configuration** tab.
5. In the list of files displayed on the left, click **kv.conf** and click Display Content on the right.
Press Ctrl+F to search for `region` and `internet-domain` . Replace ${global:region} with the `region` value and ${global:internet-domain} with the `internet-domain` value.

**Method 2: Search for the endpoint in the Apsara Infrastructure**

**Management console**

OP to make API calls

page, find the ascm-A-xxx cluster, and then click **Cluster Details** in the Actions column.
2. n the Services tab of the cluster details page, enter **ascm-brm** in the Service search box,
find the ascm-brm service, and then click **Details** in the Actions column.
3. On the service details page, click **Manage#** in the Components section. Then, click the
**Resources** tab in the Information of Component Manage# section.
4. Search for the resource named **ascm-aliyun-com-dns**, click the icon in the **Resource**
**Application Parameters** column to display detailed parameter settings, and then view
the value of **domain**.

### 2.2 Obtain an SDK of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console

**Uni-manager Management Console**

To call API operations by using the Portable OpenAPI Proxy (POP) gateway in the Apsara Unimanager Management Console, you must use an SDK. To obtain the recommended SDK version and sample code, perform the following steps: Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. In the top navigation bar, choose
**Products** > **Development Tools** > **API & SDK** > **OpenAPI Explorer**. On the page that
appears, choose **API Integration** > **SDK Sample Code**. On the SDK Examples tab, view the recommended SDK version and sample code.

> **Note:** We recommend that you use an SDK for Java, Python, or Go. If you use SDKs for other programming languages, the SDKs may be incompatible with your system.

An AccessKey pair or a Security Token Service (STS) AccessKey pair is obtained. For more information, see Obtain AccessKey credentials. The endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console is obtained. For information about how to obtain the endpoint, see Obtain service endpoints.

**Install the SDK for Go**

Alibaba Cloud SDK for Go supports Go 1.10.x or later. You can run the following command to download and install the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Go:

```
go get -u github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk
```

If a network error occurs, you can use one of the following methods to download the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Go: Use the official download method.

```
GOPROXY=https://goproxy.cn,direct go get -u github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/s
```

`dk` Use a proxy server.

```
go env -W GOPROXY='https://goproxy.cn,direct'
```

> **Important:** Keep code that contains your AccessKey pair or STS AccessKey pair confidential. For example, do not commit the code to public GitHub projects. Otherwise, your account may be compromised.

```xml
<yourStsToken> with your security token.
```

**Handle errors**

When you use the SDK for Go, a ClientError or a ServerError is returned if an error occurs on the server or SDK. Both error types are included in sdk.errors. The errors conform to the standard Go error interface and can be handled in a similar manner as standard Go errors.

**Error handling**

You can use the following code to handle errors:

```
response,err := ecsClient.DescribeInstances(request) if err != nil {
    // Obtain the error information.
   err.Error()
```

`}`

**ClientError**

When you send a request, if an error occurs on the SDK and cannot be automatically handled, the SDK returns a **ClientError**. The following code shows how to identify and obtain the error message in the ClientError:

> **Important:** When you use a specific error struct, you must add the error package
> `github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk/errors` by using the following code:

```java
package main import (
    "github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk/requests"
    // The error package that you want to add.
    "github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk/errors"
    "fmt"
```

`)` OP to make API calls

```
response, err := client.ProcessCommonRequest(request) if clientError, ok := err.(*errors.ClientError); ok{
    // Obtain the error code.
    clientError.ErrorCode()
    // Obtain the error message.
    clientError.Message()
    // Obtain the original error. The return value may be nil.
    clientError.OriginError()
```

`}`

**ServerError**

When the server returns an error message, the SDK wraps the message into a ServerError and returns it to the client. In this case, you can still obtain the original HTTP response from the response. The following code shows how to identify and obtain the error message in the ServerError and response:

> **Important:** When you use a specific error struct, you must add the error package
> `github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk/errors` by using the following code:

```java
package main import (
    "github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk/requests"
    // The error package that you want to add.
    "github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk/errors"
    "fmt"
```

`)`

```
response, err := client.ProcessCommonRequest(request) if serverError, ok := err.(*errors.ServerError); ok{
    // Obtain the error code.
    serverError.ErrorCode()
    // Obtain the error message.
    serverError.Message()
    // Obtain the original HTTP response.
    response.GetOriginHttpResponse()
```

`}`

###### 3.1.1.1.1 CreateOrganization

Creates an organization.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/organization/add HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posi tion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| name | String | Body | Yes | ascm-test | The name of the organization. |
| parentId | Integer | Body | Yes | 1 | The ID of the parent organization. You can call the GetOrganizationList operation to query organization IDs. Note The ID of the root organization is 1. |
| orgParentUuid | String | Body | No | org- 101bbf866a93 0ae6******** | The UUID of the parent organization. |
| orgUuid | String | Body | No | org- 101bbf866a93 0ae6******** | The UUID of the organization. The system automatically generates a value for this parameter. |

| multiCloudStat us | String | Body | No | null | The multi-cloud status of the organization. Default value: null. Valid values: master: The organization is a primary-cloud organization. slave: The organization is a secondary-cloud organization. null: The organization is not a multi-cloud organization. Note This parameter is deprecated. However, this parameter must be retained based on the compatibility requirements. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| extraInfo | String | Body | No | null | The additional information. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. Valid values: 200: The call was successful. 400: The organization name is left empty. The ID of the parent organization is left empty. The parent organization does not exist. The AccessKey pair is invalid. The parameter is invalid. 403: You do not have the required permissions. 500: A remote call error occurred. An internal error occurred. |
| cost | Integer | 10000 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: millisecond. |

| data | Struct |   | The returned data. |
|---|---|---|---|
| alias | String | test | The alias of the organization. The alias of an organization is automatically generated. In most cases, the alias of an organization is the name of the organization. |
| ctime | Long | 1606791494471 | The time when the organization was created. |
| cuserId | String | admin | The username of the user who created the organization. |
| extraInfo | String | null | The additional information returned. |
| id | Integer | 1 | The organization ID. |
| internal | Boolean | false | Indicates whether the organization is a preset organization. Note The system automatically generates a preset organization. The preset organization is used as the default organization. |
| level | String | 0.1 | The level of the organization. Note The level of the root organization is 0, and the levels of level-1 organizations are 0.1. 1 in 0.1 indicates that the ID of the parent organization of level-1 organizations is 1. In this case, the parent organization is the root organization. All levels follow the same rule. For example, if the ID of a level-1 organization is 3, the level of its sub-organization is 0.1.3. |

| mtime | Long | 1606791494471 | The time when the organization was last modified. Note In the scenario in which you create an organization, the system returns the same value for the mtime and ctime parameters. |
|---|---|---|---|
| multiCloudStat us | String | master | The multi-cloud status of the organization. Valid values: master: The organization is a primary- cloud organization. slave: The organization is a secondary- cloud organization. This parameter is returned only in multi- cloud scenarios. |
| muserId | String | admin | The username of the user who modified the organization. |
| name | String | test | The name of the organization. |
| parentId | Integer | 1 | The ID of the parent organization. Note The ID of the root organization is 1. |
| supportRegion List | List | ["cn-qingdao- env17-d01"] | The region IDs. Note This parameter takes effect only for level-1 organizations. If a level-1 organization is created, the ID of the central region is returned for this parameter. If a level-2 organization or its sub-organization is created, no value is returned for this parameter. |
| supportRegion s | String | cn-qingdao-env17- d01 | The region IDs. |
| uuid | String | 1231 | The UUID of the organization. |

| message | String | success | The returned message. Valid values: success: The call was successful. Can't find user by specified accessKey: No user is found by using the AccessKey pair. Caller is not the parent of user: xxx: You do not have sufficient permissions. Calling manage returns empty body: No results are returned for the call. |
|---|---|---|---|
| pureListData | Boolean | true | Indicates whether only data was returned. Note This parameter is deprecated. |
| redirect | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was redirected. Valid values: true false |
| requestId | String | 16d09b14-8a59- ****-****- 7536fe897b66 | The request ID. |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. Valid values: true false |

###### 3.1.1.1.3 GetOrganizationList

Queries a list of sub-organizations of an organization.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/organization/queryList HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posi tion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| id | Integer | Body | No | 1 | The organization ID. Note The ID of the root organization is 1. If you set the value of this parameter to the ID of an organization, sub-organizations of the organization are returned. |

| name | String | Body | No | test | The organization name. Note If id and name are specified, the id parameter has a higher priority than the name parameter. In this case, sub- organizations of the organization are returned. If only name is specified, only the organization is returned its sub- organizations are not returned. If id and name are not specified, the response is empty. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

###### 3.1.1.2.5 ListResourceGroup

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

```
POST /ascm/auth/resource_group/list_resource_group HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posi tion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| resourceGroup Name | String | Body | No | test | The name of the resource set that you want to query. If you specify only the organizationId parameter, the system returns resource sets that belong to the organization and are visible to your account. If you specify only the resourceGroupName parameter, the system returns resource sets whose names contain the specified value and that are visible to your account. |
| organizationId | Integer | Body | No | 1 | The organization ID. You can call the GetOrganizationList operation to query organization IDs. Note Only resource sets in the specified organization are returned. Resource sets in the sub- organizations of the specified organization are not returned. If you leave this parameter empty or set this parameter to 1, the system returns all resource sets that are visible to your account. |

###### 3.1.1.2.6 ListResourceGroupByAscmUserId

Queries the resource sets that are bound to a user.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/resource_group/list_resource_group_by_ascmuser_id HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posi tion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ascmuser id _ | Integer | Body | Yes | 5 | The user ID. You can call the ListUsers operation to query user IDs. Note |
| ascmRoleId | Integer | Body | No | 2 | The role ID. You can call the ListActiveRoles operation to query role IDs. If you specify this parameter, this operation returns the resource sets that are bound to the specified role of the user. ###### 3.1.1.3.6 SetDefaultRole

Specifies a default role for a user. A user can be assigned multiple roles. If a default role is specified for a user, the default role is automatically used when the user logs on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console next time. After logon, the user can switch to a different role on the User Information page or the Home page.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/role/setDefaultRole HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posi tion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| loginName | String | Body | No | testu | The logon name of the user. Note If this parameter is left empty, the logon name of the current user is used by default. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| roleId | Integer | Body | Yes | 2 | The role ID. You can call the ListActiveRoles operation to query role IDs. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. Valid values: 200: The call was successful. 403: You do not have the required permissions. 404: The user does not exist. The role does not exist. The role does not belong to your account. 500: An internal error occurred. |
| cost | Integer | 10000 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: millisecond. |
| message | String | success | The returned message. Valid values: success: The request was successful. Forbidden: You do not have the required permissions. NotExist: The user does not exist. The role does not exist. The role does not belong to your account. InternalServerError: An internal error occurred. |

| pureListData | Boolean | false | Indicates whether only data was returned. Valid values: Note This parameter is deprecated. |
|---|---|---|---|
| redirect | Boolean | false | Indicates whether the request was redirected. Valid values: true false |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. Valid values: true false |

**Examples**

Sample request

```
POST /ascm/auth/role/setDefaultRole HTTP/1.1
```

`{`

```json
    "loginName": "testu",
    "roleId": 2
```

`}` Sample success responses `XML` format

```xml
<redirect>false</redirect> <cost>10000</cost> <code>200</code> <success>true</success> <message>success</message>
```

`JSON` format `{`

```json
    "cost": 10000,
    "code": 200,
```
```json
    "success": true,
    "message": "success"
```

`}`

###### 3.1.1.4.2 AddUser

Creates a user.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

###### 3.1.1.4.3 DeactivateUser

Disables a user. If you disable a user, all AccessKey pairs of the user are automatically disabled. Apsara Stack V3.12.0 SP016 and later support this operation. Apsara Stack V3.14.0 SP013 and later support this operation.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/deactivateUser HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posi tion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| loginName | String | Body | Yes | testuser2022 | The logon name of the user. |

Valid values: 200: The call was successful. 401: The user is not authenticated. 400: One or more parameters are invalid. 402: The cookie is invalid. 403: The operation is prohibited. Access to a specific resource is prohibited. 404: The resource that you want to access does not exist. 406: The account is not enabled. 409: The resource that you want to save or add already exists. 418: The verification based on a verification code failed. 419: The third-party service authentication failed. 420: The signature verification failed. 421: The certificate verification failed. 425: The service does not exist. 426: The certificate does not exist. 427: The AccessKey pair is valid. However, the user to whom the AccessKey pair belongs cannot perform this operation. 428: The AccessKey pair is invalid, does not exist, or is in an abnormal state. 500: An internal error occurred. ###### 3.1.1.4.4 GetUserInfo

Queries the information about a user.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/getUserInfo HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| loginName | String | Body | No | testuser2022 | The logon name of the user. Note The loginName parameter takes precedence over the userAccessKeyId and pk parameters. If you specify a logon name that does not exist, the system returns an error that indicates the user does not exist. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| userAccessKey Id | String | Body | No | UyAna7V7RG* ***** | The AccessKey ID of the user. Note If you do not specify the loginName parameter, you can leave the loginName parameter empty. If you do not specify the longinName and userAccessKeyId parameters, the operation is performed based on the pk parameter. |
| pk | String | Body | No | 25925866254 4****** | The primary key of the account. Note If only the pk parameter is specified, the operation is performed based on the pk parameter. If the loginName or userAccessKeyId parameter is specified, you can leave the pk parameter empty. If no request parameters are specified, an error is returned. |

###### 3.1.1.4.5 ListAccessKeysForManagedUsers

Queries AccessKey pairs of users that are managed by the user who calls this operation. You can use the ascmUserId, organizationId, and loginName parameters to specify the organization and users that you want to query. If you do not specify the parameters, the AccessKey pairs of all users that are managed by the user who calls this operation is returned. A platform administrator, such as a super administrator, and a resource inspector can query the AccessKey pairs of all users. Other global roles, such as the admin role, can query the AccessKey pairs of users who do not belong to internal organizations. Organization administrators or other roles who have the management permissions on the organization and its sub-organizations can query the AccessKey pairs of users in the current organization and its sub-organizations.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Syntax**

```
POST /user/accesskey/listAccessKeysForManagedUsers HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

###### 3.1.1.4.6 DeleteUserAccessKey

Deletes the AccessKey pairs of a user. Make sure that a user has at least one AccessKey in the ACTIVE state after you delete the AccessKey pairs of the user. You can manage the AccessKey pairs of your account. The super administrator can manage the AccessKey pairs of all users. Other global roles such as the admin role can manage the AccessKey pairs of users who do not belong to internal organizations. Organization administrators or other roles who have the management permissions on the organization and its sub-organizations can manage the AccessKey pairs of users in the current organization and its sub-organizations.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.


**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. |
| message | String | success | The returned message. |
| cost | Long | 107 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: millisecond. |

###### 3.1.1.4.7 UpdateUserAccessKeyStatus

Enables or disables a single AccessKey pair. Make sure that at least one AccessKey pair is enabled after you enable or disable a single AccessKey pair. Otherwise, an error is reported for this operation. You can manage the AccessKey pairs of your account. The super administrator can manage the AccessKey pairs of all users. Other global roles such as the admin role can manage the AccessKey pairs of users who do not belong to internal organizations. ###### 3.1.1.4.8 CreateUserAccessKey

Creates an AccessKey pair for a user. Each user can have up to two AccessKey pairs. You can call the CreateUserAccessKey operation to create an AccessKey pair for your account. An AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret are returned. The super administrator can create AccessKey pairs for all users and only AccessKey IDs are returned. Other global roles such as the admin role can create AccessKey pairs for users who do not belong to internal organizations. Only AccessKey IDs are returned. Organization administrators or other roles who have the management permissions on the organization and its sub-organizations can create AccessKey pairs for users in the current organization and its sub-organizations. Only AccessKey IDs are returned.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

```
POST /user/accessKey HTTP/1.1
```

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| loginName | Strin g | Body | No | Test | The username of the user for which you want to create an AccessKey pair. If you do not specify this parameter, an AccessKey pair is created for your account. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. |
| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. |
| message | String | success | The returned message. |
| cost | Long | 100 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: millisecond. |
| data | Struct | - | The information about the created AccessKey pair. |
| -accesskeyId | String | qwe****** | The AccessKey ID. |
| - accesskeySecr et | String | eb2hf****** | The AccessKey secret. |
| -status | String | ACTIVE | The status of the AccessKey pair. Default value: ACTIVE, which indicates that the AccessKey pair is enabled. |
| -ctime | Long | 1715835495000 | The time when the AccssKey pair of the user was created. |

###### 3.1.1.4.9 GetRecentAkTrailForUser

Queries the audit logs of AccessKey pairs of a user. You can query the logs of disabled AccessKey pairs. You cannot query the logs of deleted AccessKey pairs. The AccessKey pair logs have a latency of about 1 hour in most cases. By default, logs are stored for only seven days. Exercise caution when you change your AccessKey pair. If you want to save logs for a longer period of time, you must configure log storage settings to store logs in Simple Log Service.

###### 3.1.1.4.13 ListUsers

Queries users that are visible to the operation caller.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posi tion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| loginName | String | Body | No | testuser | The logon name of the user. The logon name must be 2 to 64 characters in length and can contain letters, digits, underscores ( ), hyphens (-), and _ periods (.). Note If this parameter is specified, a fuzzy query is performed based on the specified logon name. If no parameters are specified, all users that are visible to the operation caller are returned. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| roleId | Integer | Body | No | 6 | The role ID. You can call the ListActiveRoles operation to query role IDs. Note If this parameter is specified, the users that are visible to the operation caller and bound to the specified role are returned. |
| loginPolicyId | Integer | Body | No | 1084 | The ID of the logon policy. You can call the ListActiveRoles operation to query logon policy IDs. Note If this parameter is specified, the users that are visible to the operation caller and bound to the specified logon policy are returned. |
| organizationId | Integer | Body | No | 25 | The organization ID. You can call the ListActiveRoles operation to query organization IDs. Note If this parameter is specified, the users that are visible to the operation caller and belong to the specified organization are returned. |

| currentPage | Integer | Body | No | 1 | The page number. Default value: 1. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pageSize | Integer | Body | No | 10 | The number of entries per page. Default value: 10. |
| status | String | Body | No | active | The status of the user. Valid values: active inactive |

###### 3.1.1.4.14 ListUsersInsideRole

Queries all users that are bound to a role.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/listUsersInsideRole HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posi tion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| organizationId | Integer | Body | No | 3 | The ID of the organization to which the users belong. You can call the GetOrganizationList operation to query organization IDs. Note If you specify a value for organizationId, only users that belong to the organization are returned. You can leave this parameter empty. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| currentPage | Integer | Body | No | 1 | The page number. Default value: 1. |
| pageSize | Integer | Body | No | 10 | The number of entries per page. |
| loginName | String | Body | No | test | The SQL regular expression for logon names of the users. Note If you specify this parameter, users that are associated with the role and meet the specified regular expression condition are returned. If you do not specify this parameter, all users that are associated with the role are returned. |
| roleId | Integer | Body | Yes | 1 | The ID of the role assigned to the user. You can call the ListRoles operation to query role IDs. |

###### 3.1.1.4.15 LockUser

Locks a specific user. After you lock a user, you cannot modify the attributes of the user.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/lockUser HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| id | Integ er | Body | No | 3 | The user ID. You need to configure either loginName or id to specify the user that you want to lock. |

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| loginNam e | Strin g | Body | No | testuser | The logon name of the user. You need to configure either loginName or id to specify the user that you want to lock. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. |
| cost | Integer | 1000 | The amount of time that is consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. |
| message | String | success | The returned message. |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. |

**Examples**

Sample requests

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/lockUser HTTP/1.1
```

`{`

```json
    "loginName": "testuser"
```

`}` Sample success responses `JSON` format `{`

```json
 "code":"200",
 "cost":1000,
 "success":true,
 "message":"success"
```

`}` `XML` format

```xml
<code>200</code> <cost>1000</cost> <success>true</success> <message>success</message>
```

###### 3.1.1.4.17 RecoverUserByLoginName

Recover a deleted user.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | RecoverUserByL oginName | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to RecoverUserByLoginName. |
| LoginName | String | Yes | testtest | The logon name of the user. |
| OrganizationId | Integer | Yes | 5 | The organization ID. |
| roleIdList | Json | No | {"RoleIdList": [ "5", "6", "8" ]} | The roles. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| loginNam e | Strin g | Body | No | testuser | The logon name of the user. You must specify the user that you want to associate with the external system by configuring one of the id and loginName parameters in the request. |

###### 3.1.1.4.22 ResetPasswordByLoginName

Resets the password of a user. Only administrators of an organization can reset the password of a user in the organization. You can call the ResetPasswordByLoginName operation to reset the password of a user to a random password. You can perform the following steps to view the random password in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console: In the top navigation bar, click Enterprise. In the left-side navigation pane, choose Users > Users. On the Users page, find the user whose password you reset and click the username to go to the User Details page. On the User Details, view the password of the user. When the user uses the random password to log on for the first time, the user is required to change the random password. If you use Apsara Stack V3.17.0 or later, we recommend that you use the ResetUserPasswordByLoginName operation instead of the ResetPasswordByLoginName operation.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/resetPasswordByLoginName HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posi tion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| loginName | String | Body | Yes | testu | The logon name of the user. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. Valid values: 200: The call was successful. 403: You do not have the required permissions. 404: The user does not exist. 500: An internal error occurred. |
| cost | Integer | 10000 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: millisecond. |

| message | String | success | The returned message. Valid values: success: The call was successful. Forbidden: You do not have the required permissions. NotExist: The user does not exist. InternalServerError: An internal error occurred. |
|---|---|---|---|
| pureListData | Boolean | false | Indicates whether only data was returned. Note This parameter is deprecated. |
| redirect | Boolean | false | Indicates whether the request was redirected. Valid values: true false |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. Valid values: true false |

**Examples**

Sample requests

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/resetPasswordByLoginName HTTP/1.1 Common request parameters
```

`{`

```json
    "loginName": "testu"
```

`}` Sample success responses `XML` format

```xml
<redirect>false</redirect> <cost>10000</cost> <code>200</code> <success>true</success> <message>success</message>
```

```json
    "cost": 10000,
    "code": 200,
    "success": true,
    "message": "success"
```

###### 3.1.1.5.7 ListUsersInUserGroup

Queries users in a user group.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/listUsersInUserGroup HTTP/1.1
```

###### 3.1.1.6.2 CheckLoginPolicy

Checks whether the logon policy associated with a user is enabled during a simulated logon to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. You can call the CheckLoginPolicy operation to check whether the logon policy associated with a user is enabled during a simulated logon to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/loginPolicy/checkLoginPolicy HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posi tion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| loginName | String | Body | Yes | WFAdmin | The logon name of the user. |
| ip | String | Body | Yes | 192.168.1.0 | The logon IP address. An IP address can be associated with one of the following types of logon policies: logon policies for which a whitelist is configured and logon policies for which a blacklist is configured. |
| time | Long | Body | No | 16624468634 45 | The logon timestamp. The default value is the current timestamp of the system. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. Valid values: 200: The call was successful. 401: The user is not authenticated. 400: One or more parameters are invalid. 402: The cookie is invalid. 403: The operation is prohibited. Access to a specific resource is prohibited. 404: The resource that you want to access does not exist. 406: The account is not enabled. 409: The resource that you want to save or add already exists. 418: The verification based on a verification code failed. 419: The third-party service authentication failed. 420: The signature verification failed. 421: The certificate verification failed. 425: The service does not exist. 426: The certificate does not exist. 427: The AccessKey pair is valid. However, the user to whom the AccessKey pair belongs cannot perform this operation. 428: The AccessKey pair is invalid, does not exist, or is in an abnormal state. 500: An internal error occurred. This code is returned if an unidentified exception occurred. 511: The parameter value exceeds the defined threshold. 512: The security token issued by STS is invalid. 513: The dependent service is abnormal. |
|---|---|---|---|
| cost | Integer | 7 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: millisecond. |

| data | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the user passed the logon policy check. Valid values: true: The user passed the logon policy check. For example, if the user is associated with a logon IP address blacklist policy, and the logon IP address is not in the blacklist, true is returned for the data parameter. false: The user failed to pass the logon policy check. For example, if the user is associated with a logon IP address blacklist policy, and the logon IP address is in the blacklist, false is returned for the data parameter. |

| message | String | success | The returned message. Note This parameter is returned, regardless of whether the request was successful. ##### 3.1.2.5 GetEnterpriseCenterQuota

Queries the quota limits in the enterprise center. The enterprise center allows you to query 12 quota limits. After the call is successful, information about the quota limits and the maximum values of metrics on the cloud platform is returned. MaxResourceSetBindAscmUserLimit: the maximum number of users that can be associated with a resource set. MaxResourceSetBindAscmUserGroupLimit: the maximum number of user groups that can be associated with a resource set. MaxUserGroupCanJoinUserLimit: the maximum number of users that can be added to a user group. MaxUserAddUserGroupLimit: the maximum number of user groups that a user can be added to. MaxUserAddResourceSetLimit: the maximum number of resource sets that a role of a user can be added to. MaxUserGroupAddResourceLimit: the maximum number of resource sets that a user group can be added to. MaxRoleBindAscmUserLimit: the maximum number of roles that can be associated with a user. MaxRoleAuthorizationBindAscmUserLimit: the maximum number of RAM roles that can be associated with a user. MaxRoleBindAscmUserGroupLimit: the maximum number of roles that can be associated with a user group. MaxPolicyLimit: the maximum number of custom policies that can be created per Alibaba Cloud account. MaxRamGroupLimit: the maximum number of RAM groups that can be created per Alibaba Cloud account. MaxRamRoleLimit: the maximum number of RAM roles that can be created per Alibaba Cloud account.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/stat/enterpriseCenterQuota HTTP/1.1
```

This operation does not have operation-specific request parameters.

**Response parameters**

|---|---|---|---|
| data | Normal | [{"current": 35,"displayName": "\u8d44\u6e90\u96 c6\u7ed1\u5b9a\u7 684\u6700\u5927\ u7528\u6237\u4e2 a\u6570","hasDetai l": true,"item": "MaxResourceSetBi ndAscmUserLimit", "quota": 10000,"updateTim e": 1692013092000}] | 12 quota limits are returned in a list, which contains the following fields: item: the limit item. current: the actual maximum value of the current item. displayName: the display field. hasDetail: indicates whether details are shown. quota: the quota of the limit item. updateTime: the timestamp of the last update. |
| dynamicMessa ge | String | [] | The dynamic prompt information. |
| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. |
| cost | Integer | 150 | The amount of time that is consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. |
| message | String | success | The returned message. |

##### 3.1.2.6 GetEnterpriseCenterQuotaDetail

Queries the detailed information about the users, user groups, resource sets, or Apsara Stack tenant accounts that have exceeded the preset enterprise quota or the specified quantity limits. You can call this operation to query the detailed information about the users, user groups, resource sets, or Apsara Stack tenant accounts that have exceeded the specified quota in the Enterprise module of Apsara Uni-manger or the quantity limits you specified in the request parameters.

**Request headers**

The SetIdPConfig operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/stat/enterpriseCenterQuotaDetail HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posit ion | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| type | Strin g | Body | No | MaxResourceSetBindAsc mUserLimit | The quota items in the Enterprise module of Apsara Uni-manger: MaxResourceSetBindAs cmUserLimit: the maximum number of users that can be bound to a resource set. MaxResourceSetBindAs cmUserGroupLimit: the maximum number of user groups that can be bound to a resource set. MaxUserGroupCanJoin UserLimit: the maximum number of users that can be added to a user group. MaxUserAddUserGroup Limit: the maximum number of user groups that a user can join. MaxUserAddResourceS etLimit: the maximum number of resource sets to which a user- specified role can be bound. MaxUserGroupAddReso urceLimit: the maximum number of resource sets to which a user group can be bound. MaxRoleBindAscmUser Limit: the maximum number of roles that can be bound to a user. MaxRoleAuthorizationB indAscmUserLimit: the maximum number of authorized RAM roles that can be bound to a user. MaxRoleBindAscmUser GroupLimit: the maximum number of roles that can be bound to a user group. |

|   |   |   |   |   | MaxPolicyLimit: the maximum number of custom policies that can be created in an Apsara Stack tenant account. MaxRamGroupLimit: the maximum number of RAM groups that can be created in an Apsara Stack tenant account. MaxRamRoleLimit: the maximum number of RAM roles that can be created in an Apsara Stack tenant account. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| limit | Integ er | Body | No | 100 | The quantity limits for the users, user groups, resource sets, or Apsara Stack tenant accounts that you want to query. If you leave this parameter empty, users, user groups, resource sets, or Apsara Stack tenant accounts that exceed the specified quota in the Enterprise module of Apsara Uni-manger will be returned. |
| currentPag e | Integ er | Body | No | 1 | The page number. Default value: 1. |
| pageSize | Integ er | Body | No | 10 | The number of entries per page. Valid values: 1 to 500. Default value: 10. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| data | Normal | [{"active":true,"co unt":13,"id":40617, "loginName":"ramu seriiiz","updateTim e":1692013097000 ,"username":"ramu seriiiz"}] | The returned data based on the value you specified for the type parameter. For more information, see the "Supplementary details of the data parameter" section of this topic. |

| dynamicMessa ge | String | [] | The dynamic prompt information. |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The response code. |
| cost | Integer | 17 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. |
| message | String | "success" | The returned message. |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. Valid values: true and false. |
| successRespo nse | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. Valid values: true and false. |
| pageInfo | Struct |   | The pagination information. |
| -currentPage | Integer | 1 | The page number. |
| -pageSize | Integer | 10 | The number of entries per page. |
| -total | Integer | 9629 | The total number of entries returned. |
| -totalPage | Integer | 963 | The total number of pages returned. |

**Supplementary details of the data parameter**

If you set the type parameter to MaxUserAddUserGroupLimit, MaxUserAddResourceSetLimit, MaxRoleBindAscmUserLimit, or MaxRoleAuthorizationBindAscmUserLimit, the details of the user (UserEntry) type are returned. The details contain the following fields:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| id | Integer | The user ID. |
| username | String | The display name of the user. |
| loginName | String | The logon name of the user. |
| isActive | Boolean | Indicates whether the user is active. |

| roleId | Integer | The default role ID. |
|---|---|---|
| roleName | String | The default role name. |
| count | Integer | The actual quantity of the item you queried. |
| updateTime | Timestamp | The time of the last update. The value is a UNIX timestamp. |

If you set the type parameter to MaxUserGroupCanJoinUserLimit, MaxUserGroupAddResourceLimit, or MaxRoleBindAscmUserGroupLimit, the details of the user group (UserGroupEntry) type are returned. The details include the following fields:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| id | Integer | The ID of the user group. |
| augId | String | The UUID of the user group. |
| groupName | String | The name of the user group. |
| organizationName | String | The name of the organization to which the user group belongs. |
| count | Integer | The actual quantity of the item you queried. |
| updateTime | Timestamp | The time of the last update. The value is a UNIX timestamp. |

If you set the type parameter to MaxResourceSetBindAscmUserLimit or MaxResourceSetBindAscmUserGroupLimit, the details of the resource set (ResourceSetEntry) type are returned. The details include the following fields:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| id | Integer | The ID of the resource set. |
| rsId | String | The UUID of the resource set. |
| resourceGroupName | String | The name of a resource set. |

| organizationName | String | The name of the organization to which the resource set belongs. |
|---|---|---|
| count | Integer | The actual quantity of the item you queried. |
| updateTime | Timestamp | The time of the last update. The value is a UNIX timestamp. |

If you set the type parameter to MaxPolicyLimit, MaxRamGroupLimit, or MaxRamRoleLimit, the details of the Apsara Stack tenant account (RamEntry) type are returned. The details include the following fields:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| aliyunId | Integer | The ID of the Apsara Stack tenant account. |
| accountKp | String | The primary key of the Apsara Stack tenant account. The primary key is used as the UID of the account. |
| organizationName | String | The name of the organization to which the Apsara Stack tenant account belongs. |
| count | Integer | The actual quantity of the item you queried. |
| updateTime | Timestamp | The time of the last update. The value is a UNIX timestamp. |

**Examples**

```
POST /ascm/auth/stat/enterpriseCenterQuotaDetail HTTP/1.1
```

##### 3.1.3.7 UpdateInstanceBelong

Changes the resource set of an instance. You cannot change the resource set of an instance across level-1 organizations. When you call this operation, the system checks whether the quota limits of resource sets and instances are reached. If so, the error code 510 is returned. The security groups of Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances and the vSwitches in the virtual private clouds (VPCs) can be changed only within the sharing scope of the VPC to which they belong. If you change the resource set of an ECS instance, the disks, snapshots, and elastic network interfaces (ENIs) of the ECS instance are also changed. If you change the resource set of a VPC, the route tables in the VPC are also changed.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the Common parameters topic.

**Request syntax**

```
POST /ascm/manage/belong/updateInstance HTTP/1.1
```

| RegionNa me | Strin g | Body | Yes | cn-****-d01 | The region ID of the instance. |
| TargetRes ourceSetId | Strin g | Body | No | 2 | The ID of the destination resource set. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. Valid values: true false |
| Code | String | 200 | The response code. 200: The request was successful 400: The resource type is invalid. The specified resource set is not found. The specified instance ID is invalid. You cannot change the resource set of an instance across level-1 organizations. Change failed. 403: You do not have permissions. 510: The quota limit is reached. |
| Message | String | exampleerrmessag e | The response. If the request was successful, a null value is returned. If the request failed, an error message is returned. |
| RequestId | String | 530dxxx-dxx******- x6b61axxxxx | The ID of the request to change the resource set of an instance. |
| ErrorKey | String | exampleErrKey | The error code. |
| Cost | Long | 934 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: milliseconds. |
| Path | String | examplepath | The request path. |

#### 3.1.4 Configurations

##### 3.1.4.1 BatchCreateRAMServiceRole

Creates multiple service-linked roles at a time. You can call the ListRAMServiceRoles operation to query the created service-linked roles. A service-linked role is used by a trusted Alibaba Cloud service to access other Alibaba Cloud services or manage resources in other Alibaba Cloud services. If you create an instance of an Alibaba Cloud service that needs access to another Alibaba Cloud service, a service-linked role is automatically created for the service in the level-1 organization of the organization in which you create the instance. For example, an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance needs the permissions to create an Object Storage Service (OSS) bucket for image storage. The ECS instance needs to assume the corresponding service-linked role that is provided by OSS. This way, the ECS instance is granted permissions to manage OSS resources.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/ramServiceRole/batchCreateRAMServiceRole HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posi tion | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| organizationId List.N | Repeat List | Body | Yes | ["14","18","19" ,"21","23","24" ] | The organization IDs. Separate multiple organization IDs with commas (,). You can call the GetOrganizationTree operation to query organization IDs. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| productName | String | Body | Yes | NAS | The name of the service. You can call the ListRAMServiceRoleProducts operation to query service names. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. Valid values: 200: The call was successful. 401: The user is not authenticated. 400: One or more parameters are invalid. 402: The cookie is invalid. 403: The operation is prohibited. Access to a specific resource is prohibited. 404: The resource that you want to access does not exist. 406: The account is not activated. 409: The resource that you want to save or add already exists. 418: The verification based on a verification code failed. 419: The third-party service authentication failed. 420: The signature verification failed. 421: The certificate verification failed. 425: The service does not exist. 426: The certificate does not exist. 427: The AccessKey pair is valid. However, the user to whom the AccessKey pair belongs cannot perform this operation. 428: The AccessKey pair is invalid, does not exist, or is in an abnormal state. 500: An internal error occurred. This code is returned if an unidentified exception occurred. 511: The parameter value exceeds the defined threshold. 512: The security token issued by STS is invalid. 513: The dependent service is abnormal. |
|---|---|---|---|
| cost | Integer | 22 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: millisecond. |

| message | String | success | The returned message. Note This parameter is returned, regardless of whether the request was successful. If the request was successful, success is returned as the value of this parameter. If the request failed, a custom error message or an error message in the error stack is returned. |
|---|---|---|---|
| pureListData | Boolean | false | Indicates whether only data was returned. Note This parameter is deprecated. |
| redirect | Boolean | false | Indicates whether the request was redirected. Valid values: Note This parameter is deprecated. true false |
| success | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the request was successful. Valid values: true false |

**Examples**

##### 3.1.4.2 GetPasswordPolicy

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

|---|---|---|---|

| cost | Integer | 5 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: millisecond. |
| data | Struct |   | The password policy data. |

| hardExpiry | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password has expired. Valid values: true: The password has expired. An expired password cannot be used to log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. false: The password has not expired. Note The maxPasswordAge parameter indicates the validity period of a password. We recommend that you update your password before it expires. If your password expires, contact the operations manager or platform administrator to reset the password. |
|---|---|---|---|
| maxLoginAtte mps | Integer | 5 | The maximum number of logon attempts with an incorrect password during the password error tolerance period. Note Valid values: 0 to 32. |
| maxPassword Age | Integer | 90 | The validity period of the password. Unit: day. A value of 0 indicates that no password expiration rule is used. Note Valid values: 0 to 1095. |
| minimumPass wordLength | Integer | 10 | The minimum number of characters in a password. Note Valid values: 8 to 32. |
| passwordError CaptchaTime | Integer | 3 | The maximum number of failed logon attempts with incorrect passwords before human verification (CAPTCHA) appears. |

| passwordError LockPeriod | Integer | 30 | The duration for which the account is frozen. Unit: minutes. Note If the maximum number of failed logon attempts with incorrect passwords is reached, your account is frozen, and you cannot log on with the account within the period. Valid values: 0 to 1440. |

| passwordError TolerancePerio d | Integer | 60 | The period of time during which the maximum number of failed logon attempts are allowed. The default period of time is 60 minutes. The maxLoginAttemps parameter indicates the allowed maximum number of logon attempts with an incorrect password during the password error tolerance period. |
| passwordReus ePrevention | Integer | 5 | The number of previous passwords that cannot be reused. Default value: 0, which indicates that users can reuse any previous passwords. Note Valid values: 0 to 24. |

| requireNumbe rs | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password must contain digits. |
| requireSymbol s | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password must contain special characters. |
| requireUpperc aseCharacters | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password must contain uppercase letters. |

##### 3.1.4.8 ResetPasswordPolicy

Resets the current password policy of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. After you call this operation, the password policy is reset to the default password policy of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. To modify the password policy of the Apsara Unimanager Management Console, call the SetPasswordPolicy operation. For more information about the default password policy of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, see the returned data of this operation.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Syntax**

```
POST /ascm/auth/user/resetPasswordPolicy HTTP/1.1
```

**Request parameters**

You do not need to specify request parameters for this operation.

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | String | 200 | The HTTP status code. Valid values: 200: The call was successful. 500: An internal error occurred. This code is returned if an unidentified exception occurred. |

| cost | Integer | 14 | The amount of time consumed by the operation. Unit: millisecond. |
|---|---|---|---|
| data | Struct |   | The password policy data. |
| hardExpiry | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password has expired. Valid values: true: The password has expired. An expired password cannot be used to log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. false: The password has not expired. Note The maxPasswordAge parameter indicates the validity period of a password. We recommend that you update your password before it expires. If your password expires, contact the operations manager or platform administrator to reset the password. |
| maxLoginAtte mps | Integer | 5 | The maximum number of logon attempts with an incorrect password during the password error tolerance period. Note Valid values: 0 to 32. |
| maxPassword Age | Integer | 90 | The validity period of the password. Unit: day. A value of 0 indicates that no password expiration rule is used. Note Valid values: 0 to 1095. |
| minimumPass wordLength | Integer | 10 | The minimum number of characters in the password. Note Valid values: 8 to 32. |
| passwordError CaptchaTime | Integer | 3 | The maximum number of failed logon attempts with incorrect passwords before human verification (CAPTCHA) appears. |

| passwordError LockPeriod | Integer | 30 | The duration for which the account is frozen. Unit: minutes. Note If the maximum number of failed logon attempts with incorrect passwords is reached, your account is frozen, and you cannot log on with the account within the period. Valid values: 0 to 1440. |
|---|---|---|---|
| passwordError TolerancePerio d | Integer | 5 | The period of time during which the maximum number of failed logon attempts are allowed. The default period of time is 60 minutes. The maxLoginAttemps parameter indicates the allowed maximum number of logon attempts with an incorrect password during the password error tolerance period. |
| passwordReus ePrevention | Integer | 5 | The number of previous passwords that cannot be reused. Default value: 0, which indicates that users can reuse any previous passwords. Note Valid values: 0 to 24. |
| requireLowerc aseCharacters | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password must contain lowercase letters. |
| requireNumbe rs | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password must contain digits. |
| requireSymbol s | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password must contain special characters. |
| requireUpperc aseCharacters | Boolean | true | Indicates whether the password must contain uppercase letters. |

| message | String | success | The returned message. Note This parameter is returned, regardless of whether the request was successful. MSSQL: ApsaraDB RDS for SQL Server instance or self- managed SQL Server database. kafka: ApsaraMQ for Kafka instance or self-managed Kafka cluster. DataHub: DataHub project. clickhouse: ApsaraDB for ClickHouse cluster. DB2: self-managed Db2 for LUW database. as400: AS/400. Tablestore: Tablestore instance. Note This parameter takes effect only for data synchronization tasks. |

## 4 STS API reference

### 4.1 AssumeRole

Obtains a Security Token Service (STS) token to assume a Resource Access Management (RAM) role.

**Request header**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" topic.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Loca tion | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DurationSe conds | Long | Quer y | No | 3600 | The validity period of the STS token. Unit: seconds. Minimum value: 900. Maximum value: the value of the MaxSessionDuration parameter. Default value: 3600. |
| Policy | Strin g | Quer y | No | {"Statement": [{"Action": ["*"],"Effect": "Allow","Resource": ["*"]}],"Version":"1"} | The policy that specifies the permissions of the returned STS token. This allows you to implement more fine-grained access control. The following descriptions provide the details: If you specify this parameter, the permissions that are granted to the STS token are the intersection of the RAM role permissions and the permissions that are specified in this parameter. If you do not specify this parameter, the STS token has all permissions of the RAM role. The value of the parameter must be 1 to 1,024 characters in length. |

PI reference

### 4.2 GetCallerIdentity

Queries the identity of the current requester.

**Request header**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" topic.
